title: Suspicious IP address
summary: Triage an IP from an alert or log: reputation, owner, exposure and related infrastructure.

steps.title: Check reputation
steps.detail: See whether the address is already known as malicious, a scanner or harmless background noise.

steps.title: Identify owner and location
steps.detail: Find the ASN, network owner and rough location. Hosting providers, VPNs and Tor exits change how you read the alert.

steps.title: See what it exposes
steps.detail: Passive scan data shows open ports, banners and certificates without touching the host.

steps.title: Pivot to related domains
steps.detail: Reverse DNS and co-hosted domains can reveal the campaign or service behind the address.

steps.title: Check threat intelligence
steps.detail: Look for reports, pulses or indicators that mention the address.

steps.title: Probe it directly (only if in scope)
steps.detail: Port scans and similar probes touch the target and leave logs on their side. Do this only with authorisation.

steps.title: Capture evidence
steps.detail: Screenshot results and keep timestamps before the data changes.

title: Phishing email or link
summary: Work through a reported phishing message: the link, the domain, the sender and any attachment.

steps.title: Expand the link safely
steps.detail: Reveal where shortened or redirecting links really go without opening them in your own browser.

steps.title: Scan the URL
steps.detail: Get a rendered screenshot, requests made and reputation verdicts from a hosted sandbox.

steps.title: Check known phishing feeds
steps.detail: See if the URL or domain has already been reported.

steps.title: Look for lookalike domains
steps.detail: Generate and check typosquats of the brand being imitated.

steps.title: Check domain age and owner
steps.detail: Newly registered domains and hidden registrants are common in phishing.

steps.title: Check the sender
steps.detail: Test the sending address, mail server reputation and whether it appears in breaches.

steps.title: Analyse attachments
steps.detail: Look up the file hash first, then detonate it in a sandbox if it is unknown.

steps.title: Preserve evidence
steps.detail: Save the page and the headers before the site is taken down.

title: Unknown file or malware sample
summary: Triage a suspicious file: hash lookup, sandboxing, format-specific checks, deobfuscation and context.

steps.title: Look up the hash
steps.detail: Search by hash first. A known sample saves you a sandbox run and avoids uploading sensitive files.

steps.title: Run it in a sandbox
steps.detail: Upload only files you are allowed to share. Hosted sandboxes may make the sample public.

steps.title: Document and script specifics
steps.detail: For Office documents, scan for malicious macros and exploits. For PDFs or Android packages, use a format-specific tool instead.

steps.title: Deobfuscate and decode
steps.detail: Unpack encoded strings, scripts and XOR-obfuscated payloads.

steps.title: Inspect network traffic
steps.detail: Review captured network traffic for command-and-control and downloads.

steps.title: Identify the family and ransomware
steps.detail: Match behaviour to known families and techniques.

steps.title: Reverse engineer (if needed)
steps.detail: Static analysis for samples that need a deeper look.

title: Domain investigation
summary: Profile a domain: registration, DNS history, subdomains, certificates, technology and reputation.

steps.title: Registration records
steps.detail: Who registered it, when, and what else do they own?

steps.title: Passive DNS history
steps.detail: See past resolutions and related infrastructure without querying the target.

steps.title: Find subdomains
steps.detail: Map the visible attack surface.

steps.title: Certificate transparency
steps.detail: Certificates reveal hostnames and related domains.

steps.title: Identify technology and ownership clues
steps.detail: Shared analytics IDs and tech stacks link sites together.

steps.title: Check reputation
steps.detail: See whether security vendors flag the domain.

steps.title: Review history
steps.detail: Compare past versions of the site.

title: Email address or identity
summary: Investigate an email address: validity, breaches, linked accounts and the organisation behind it.

steps.title: Validate the address
steps.detail: Check it exists, isn't disposable and what its reputation looks like.

steps.title: Check breaches
steps.detail: Find leaked credentials and infostealer exposure linked to the address.

steps.title: Find linked accounts
steps.detail: See which services and profiles the address is registered with.

steps.title: Understand the organisation
steps.detail: Work out the company's email format and related addresses.

steps.title: Pivot on the domain
steps.detail: Look at who owns the address's domain.

title: Vulnerability and CVE triage
summary: Assess a CVE or advisory: severity, exploit availability, exposure and attacker techniques.

steps.title: Read the advisory
steps.detail: Confirm affected versions and the vendor's severity rating.

steps.title: Check for public exploits
steps.detail: Public exploit code raises urgency.

steps.title: Measure internet exposure
steps.detail: See how many hosts run the affected software.

steps.title: Map to attacker techniques
steps.detail: Connect the vulnerability to known tactics for detection ideas.

steps.title: Check default credentials
steps.detail: For devices and appliances, default passwords are often the real risk.

title: Dark web and leak monitoring
summary: Look for mentions of your organisation on hidden services and leak sources, with safe access.

steps.title: Set up safe access
steps.detail: Use an isolated, anonymising environment before touching hidden services.

steps.title: Check for leaks first
steps.detail: Start with indexed breach data before browsing anything.

steps.title: Search hidden services
steps.detail: Find .onion content that mentions your organisation.

steps.title: Assess the service
steps.detail: Check an onion site for metadata leaks and reachability.

steps.title: Understand the landscape
steps.detail: Background and community guidance.

steps.title: Capture evidence
steps.detail: Document findings with timestamps.

title: Pre-investigation OpSec check
summary: Before you start: make sure your browser and network don't reveal who you are, and set up evidence capture.

steps.title: Test for leaks
steps.detail: Confirm your IP, DNS and WebRTC are not exposing your real identity.

steps.title: Check your browser fingerprint
steps.detail: See what a site learns about your browser.

steps.title: Use anonymising tools if the case needs it
steps.detail: Route traffic through Tor or use a dedicated environment.

steps.title: Set up evidence capture
steps.detail: Have screenshots and page saving ready before you begin.
